title: Operator mental model triage map for LLM inference incidents
author: Ava Patel
content:
Summary

This page codifies a compact mental model and step-by-step triage map for platform operators responding to LLM inference incidents (latency spikes, token surges, model misrouting, KV cache instability, and tenant quota failures). The goal is to shorten time-to-restoration and reduce cognitive load by providing: a checklist of prioritized signals, a decision tree you can run in your head or on a call, targeted remediation commands, and post-incident analysis prompts.

Audience and scope

- Primary: platform operators, oncall SREs, platform engineers.
- Secondary: runtime and serving runtime owners, solutions engineers responding to customer-facing incidents.
- Scope: incidents that originate in or materially affect the inference serving path (request ingress -> routing -> batching -> runtime execution -> response egress). Excludes application-layer prompt bugs or downstream storage-only outages unless they cascade into the serving path.

High-level mental model (one-paragraph)

Treat the LLM serving stack as four interdependent domains: Ingress & routing (front-door: auth, rate-limit, proxy), Workload shaping (batcher, allocator, KV prefix cache), Runtime execution (model kernels, GPU utilization, quantization fallback), and Economics/tenancy (tenant quotas, burst credits). When an alert fires, quickly categorize which domain(s) show primary signal and then apply the triage checklist tied to that domain.

One-line escalation heuristics

1) If token latency p50/p95/p99 increases sharply across >20% of tenants within 3 minutes -> treat as global routing/allocator or runtime saturation issue; page runtime oncall.
2) If a single tenant sees token cost or quota hits with normal system health -> page customer success and tenant-ops; treat as tenant-config or abuse.
3) If errors (500s) spike with model-variant-swaps in logs -> treat as model onboarding/compatibility misroute; page model-platform.

Primary signals (ordered by operator priority)

- Alert names to scan first: ALERT_TOKEN_LATENCY_SPIKE, ALERT_BATCH_BACKPRESSURE, ALERT_KV_MISS_STORM, ALERT_TENANT_QUOTA_EXHAUSTION.
- Dashboards: p95 token latency by region/model, Batch occupancy & wait time, GPU util / SM stalls, KV prefix cache hit rate, Routing error rate (5xx/4xx).
- Traces to inspect: request path trace (proxy -> batch-router -> runtime-proxy -> model-exec -> cache.lookup). Look for long spans in batch-router.wait or runtime.exec.

Quick triage checklist (5-minute fast path)

1) Confirm scope: are multiple regions affected? Run: curl -s 'https://observability/api/query?expr=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[1m])) by (region))'
2) Check batcher queue depth and tail wait-time: run the latest dashboard or query: sum(batch_queue_depth) by (zone) and batch_wait_seconds:95th.
3) Inspect GPU and node allocation: k9s/launcher -> check node-pools for preemption and OOMKill events; query allocator metrics: allocator_free_gpus, allocator_retries.
4) KV cache health: kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate (should be > 0.85 for steady state), check transient miss storms.
5) Check routing logs for model-variant fallback: search for 'fallback_to_variant' and for spikes of 'model-not-found' errors.

Decision tree (textual)

- If batch_wait_seconds:95th > 200ms and batch_queue_depth rising -> prioritize workload shaping fixes: increase burst capacity, enable soft-eviction for low-priority tenants, or temporarily reduce batching window on foreground routes.
- If GPU util > 93% and SM stall counters high -> prioritize runtime kernel-level mitigation: enable warmset, trigger soft-model-swap to a lower-cost variant, or spin temporary capacity in Dedicated pool if available.
- If kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate < 0.6 and kv write errors appear -> run cache-repair workflow (see Recovery snippets).
- If only one tenant affected and quota metrics show exhaustion -> contact tenant owner, examine request sampling for abnormal rate/patterns and apply temporary manual restriction.

Targeted remediation snippets

- Increase burst capacity (operator CLI):
  1) rctl burst-capacity allocate --pool=dedicated-regional-1 --amount=2gpus --reason="incident mitigation"
  2) Annotate the change in the incident channel.

- Shorten batching window for a route (k/v config):
  1) GET /config/routes/{route_id} -> change batching.window_ms from 50 -> 20
  2) POST /config/routes/{route_id}/reload

- Force a KV prefix cache rebuild (safe under high read load):
  1) sudo -u kvcache /opt/platform/bin/kv-rebuild --prefix=tenant-*/hot --concurrency=16 --rate-limit=5000
  2) Monitor kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate and throttle if write latency increases.

Observability queries and thresholds (examples)

- p95 token latency (global): ALERT when > 250ms for 5m across >20% of regional nodes.
- batch wait 95th: ALERT when > 200ms sustained > 3 minutes.
- kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate: WARN < 0.85, SEVERE < 0.6.
- allocator_retries: WARN if > 50/min, SEVERE if > 200/min.

Common root causes and fast mitigations

- Cause: sudden tail of long sequences causing token spend spike -> Mitigation: enable adaptive prefix-eviction and apply temporary tenant soft-throttle.
- Cause: model-variant rollout introduced new kernel path with higher SM stalls -> Mitigation: rollback variant, bump canary percentage back to 0, trigger model-platform to investigate kernel fallback.
- Cause: KV backend degraded -> Mitigation: promote read-replicas, switch cache to read-through-only mode, engage storage SRE.

Escalation matrix (one-line summary version)

- Platform Oncall (first page): page #platform-oncall @oncall -> owners for immediate triage.
- Runtime team: @runtime-oncall -> for model exec stalls, kernel failures, GPU-level errors.
- Allocator/Capacity team: @allocator-oncall -> for large-scale capacity rebalancing and burst allocations.
- Product & Customer Success: @cs-escalations -> for tenant-facing impact and coordinated customer comms.

Incident runbook snippet: global latency spike

1) T+0-2m: Accept page, confirm scope (regions, percentage of tenants). Post initial status in incident channel with dashboards and top 3 metrics.
2) T+2-8m: Execute Quick triage checklist. If batch wait and allocator are primary signals, attempt fast fixes (shorten batching window, allocate burst capacity).
3) T+8-20m: If mitigation fails and system remains degraded, trigger failover to next-compatible model variant for affected routes, open formal problem ticket and schedule postmortem.
4) T+20m+: If recovery in progress, document actions and annotate alerts to suppress noise. If unrecoverable, escalate to oncall lead and product.

Post-incident analysis checklist

- Captured artifacts: top traces (sampled), top 10 offending requests, operator actions (CLI commands, config diffs), timeline with timestamps.
- Investigation prompts: Was the root cause due to workload pattern change, deployment, or hardware degradation? Did autoscaling make a positive or negative contribution? Which SLOs were breached and which tenants were impacted?
- Postmortem template fields to fill: summary, impact, timeline, root cause, remediation plan, owners, follow-up tickets, customer comms.

Cognitive-simplification patterns (helps reduce operator load)

- Use three question framing: "Is load, locality, or runtime different?" Answering these in order usually reduces branching.
- Maintain a single pinned dashboard for oncall showing (p95 latency, batch wait p95, gpu util, kv hit rate, allocator_retries).
- Keep a short list of 3 operator commands that can be run without approvals for immediate mitigation (burst allocation, batching window change, tenant soft-throttle).

Playbook maintenance and ownership

- Document owner: Platform Oncall Documentation Guild (contact: platform-docs@redwood.com).
- Review cadence: quarterly and after any large-scale inference incident.
- When to update: any change in routing, batching algorithm, allocator behavior, KV backend or model rollout process.

Appendix A — Example incident timeline (fictional)

- 10:03 UTC: ALERT_TOKEN_LATENCY_SPIKE fires (p95 global 340ms).
- 10:04 UTC: Oncall confirms region-west is worst affected; batch_wait p95 at 410ms.
- 10:07 UTC: Operator applies batching.window_ms reduction on foreground routes (50 -> 20).
- 10:12 UTC: p95 latency drops to 180ms; batch_wait p95 drops to 90ms.
- 10:30 UTC: Root cause determined to be a sudden influx of long sequence requests from three tenants; follow-up: tenant rate-limiting and improved detection.

Appendix B — Quick reference cheat-sheet (copyable)

- Check p95 latency: dashboard -> metric p95_token_latency
- Check batch wait: metric batch_wait_seconds:95th
- Check kv health: metric kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate
- Allocate burst (cli): rctl burst-capacity allocate --pool=dedicated-regional-1 --amount=2gpus --reason="incident"

Footer

If any part of this playbook is unclear during an incident, raise it immediately on the incident channel and label the page with the improvement request. This playbook is intentionally pragmatic — keep it concise, editable, and tested in the next gameday.
